proposal.name: Draw identical posters and charts on every processor

plan.name: Draw identical posters and charts on every processor
plan.summary: Make internal/statechart render identical bytes on every processor while preserving the base branch's current arm64 output for animated posters, still posters and reader SVGs, including comparison panels. Replace exactly the operations fused by the current arm64 compiler with explicit math.FMA calls preserving their operands, signs and evaluation order, and force rounding with float64 conversions wherever other arithmetic could otherwise fuse, including across temporary assignments and inlined helpers. Pin representative arm64 output hashes, reject arm64 fused instructions without an explicit math.FMA source call, and have the ordinary package tests rerun the whole package suite with -gcflags=all=-d=fmahash=n and a recursion guard so existing CI exercises that mode automatically. Document the processor-independent rendering guarantee and validation commands in SPEC.md and docs/statecharts.md, citing the existing deterministic-rendering decisions D-0347 and D-0364; the merger records the explicit arithmetic policy as a decision. Preserve the existing rendering contracts and acceptance assertions, with no changes to receipts, dashboard identities on arm64, or #791's tests when that pull request is updated with this fix.

tests.name: TestStatechartProcessorIndependentBytes792
tests.says: Animated posters, still posters and ordinary and comparison reader SVGs retain the current arm64 bytes, and the entire statechart test suite passes with implicit fusion disabled, on every host.

tests.name: TestStatechartOnlyExplicitFMA792
tests.says: Cross-compiling the production statechart package for arm64 emits fused floating-point instructions only at explicit math.FMA calls, with the same fused instruction inventory when implicit fusion is disabled.

usage.summary: Wrote `plan.json` and two acceptance tests covering arm64 byte preservation, explicit FMA use, and fusion-disabled CI testing. The plan passed its first check; both tests fail on the unchanged base as required.
